answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits where failed proof of replication triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash of deposited funds. Each shard acts as a digital anchor to ensure data persistence within the network. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror content. Like the sweet nectar of efficiency, this process validates each byte, while an opal layer of encryption locks the integrity of shard records for a 30-day binding period.
